content: [{"id": "hdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Infrastructure", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sthdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Storage", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Four steps, in the order a file really passes through them. Every upload on this site — a patient's lab report, a partner's attachment, an avatar, a course video — is judged by the same four, because they all sit on the one File record every app on this bench shares.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Platform File Limits — in System Settings › Files, opened from the sidebar because a tile cannot open a form's tab. These are the platform's own limits, applied before anything below runs: the largest an upload may be, which file types are allowed, and whether anyone but a System Manager may upload a public file. The type list is read from there by the screener too, so a type is allowed or refused in one place rather than two. Left blank, every type is accepted — which is the platform's own default.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. File Screening — the byte-level checks the platform has not got, run before a single byte reaches storage: the file's own bytes are read to see what it really is and matched against the type its name claims, and its content is scanned by ClamAV. The byte matching needs nothing set up — the formats are recognised by the platform's own detector, so no list of signatures is kept here and none can fall out of date. What is set here is which verdicts refuse a file, where the scanner is reached and what an outage of it costs the caller, and how long a verdict is kept, and every field left blank is the shipped default, never nothing. Empty Active Channels screens nothing; screening begins on the channels listed there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Azure Blob — where the bytes come to rest once they have been accepted, and the one list of records whose attachments may be public. Everything not named in Public Attachment Doctypes is held private, whatever was ticked in the upload dialog, so a patient's document cannot be made public by choosing to. Left blank, nothing may be public and the display assets that are fetched with no session — profile photos, organisation logos, the login favicon — stop loading.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "st4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Log Settings — the platform's own daily cleanup, and the only place a retention is actually carried out. The scan log is registered there by the screening switch and trimmed at the number of days set on File Screening. While that switch is off the log is not registered at all, so verdicts already written are kept untrimmed until it is turned back on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "None of this runs until its switch is on under Automations: Storage::File::screening, Storage::File::privacy and Storage::Azure::offload each ship dormant, and each is turned on by the operator. What then happened is readable in two places. Every verdict is one row in File Scan Log, accepted as well as blocked, with the reason and the channel it arrived on — a file refused for its bytes and a file refused because the scanner could not be reached are two different rows, and only the second is worth paging anyone about. The files themselves are under Files, each showing the record it belongs to and whether it is private.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "stsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Screening", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc2", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Azure Storage", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc3", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Log Settings", "col": 4}}, {"id": "stsc4", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Files", "col": 6}}, {"id": "stsc5", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "File Scan Log", "col": 6}}, {"id": "lochdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Location", "col": 12}}, {"id": "locsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Maps", "col": 4}}, {"id": "ixhdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Indexing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ixintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The ⌘K search box every rep types into. Nothing here builds the index or decides what is searched — both are settled by the app. What is set here is the one thing the app cannot know for itself: the words this team actually uses for values the CRM already holds.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ix1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. The two switches — under Automations, and both ship dormant. Search::Index::indexing is what holds leads, notes and file names in the index and answers a search at all; nothing below is reached while it is off. Search::Query::vocabulary is what reads known words out of a typed query — a stage, a status, a product line, a group, a program, a person — and applies them as filters instead of searching for them as text. Aliases are read only while the second switch is on, so a table filled in ahead of it changes nothing and breaks nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ix2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Search Aliases — one row per word a rep types that the CRM would not otherwise recognise. The word is entered as Term and the value it stands for as Resolves To, and that value is checked against the live masters before the row is saved: a value that does not exist is refused with the nearest one named, and a value held in two different places is refused until one of them is chosen. What it was understood to be is shown back on the row, and the row points at the record rather than at its spelling, so a value renamed later is followed rather than lost. A word that is already a value in its own right is refused, because two meanings for one word narrow nothing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ixafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only the closed sets are reachable this way — a stage, a status, a product line, a group, a program, a person. A patient's name, number or id is not a value of that kind: it is matched as text by the index itself, and no row here is needed to find one. A saved alias takes effect at once, on every worker, because the cached vocabulary is dropped as the row is written.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ixsc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Search Aliases", "col": 4}}, {"id": "lshdr", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Lists", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lsintro", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The columns on a rep’s list are the record’s own, with one exception: a derived field is worked out as the list is drawn and is never stored on anything. Nothing here changes a lead or an activity — a field is added, edited or retired at any time and no data moves, because none was ever written.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ls1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Derived Fields — one row per computed column. It names the list it belongs to, what the rep sees it called, and an ordered set of buckets: a value, and the plain filters that define it. The first bucket a record matches is the value it shows, and that same order is the order the field sorts in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ls2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Proving it — every row is tried on real records before it saves, inside a trial that is rolled back. A declaration whose buckets could claim one record twice, or whose column and filter would name different records, is refused with the collision named. The trial creates nothing and leaves nothing behind, and a declaration that will not prove cannot be saved at all.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ls3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Turning it on — a row ships disabled and is inert until Enabled is ticked. Once it is, the field is offered in Filter, Sort, Group By, the column picker and the Kanban picker on that list, for every rep, with no deploy and no migration.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lsafter", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which menus carry a field is set per row under Surfaces, and nothing arrives switched on: Shown By Default is off, so the column waits to be asked for, and the quick-filter bar carries the field only once someone adds it there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lssc1", "type": "shortcut", "data": {"shortcut_name": "Derived Fields", "col": 4}}]
